items.title: Anthropic proposes a share-funded Public Benefit Fund
items.summary: Anthropic plans to allocate 5% of its shares, subject to stockholder approval, to a wholly owned public-benefit fund. For each 50% increase in valuation above a baseline, the board may allocate up to another 2%. Governance and operating milestones are still to be detailed.
items.why_it_matters: A concrete proposal for sharing AI-created value, including potential responses to labor disruption, rather than only general responsible-AI promises.
items.caveat: Company announcement, not evidence of money already distributed or independently measured benefit. The roughly 20% figure combines this plan with prior founder and employee commitments; it is not the fund's starting allocation. No IPO valuation verified or used.
items.dedup: New event; also appears in today's upstream general-news edition, so include only once in combined briefing.

items.title: Vercel makes agent-session cost and caching visible in AI Gateway logs
items.summary: A new Sessions view groups an agent's requests into conversations, exposing cost, models, providers, cache-hit rates, duration and turn-by-turn routing. Session affinity keeps later turns with the provider that handled prior turns, to reuse its prompt cache.
items.why_it_matters: Helps teams investigate agent behavior and understand spending across multi-turn workflows, an operational concern as AI moves into production.
items.caveat: Verified against the vendor changelog, not an independent benchmark. No quantified cost reduction or reliability improvement established. Session affinity defaults to text/chat; explicit session IDs can be supplied.
items.dedup: New observability feature, distinct from previously covered Vercel persistent drives, fx durable sessions, domain purchases and tsc-ts.

items.title: OpenCode follow-up: developer reports AI refusals during incident response
items.summary: OpenCode developer dax says AI models initially helped investigate its security incident, then began refusing further work; he says access to Daybreak Blue subsequently improved the situation.
items.why_it_matters: Raises a practical incident-response question: whether defensive teams have reliable, authorized assistance when ordinary model safeguards interrupt legitimate investigation.
items.caveat: First-person developer account, not an independent incident report. Do not infer which models refused, that safeguards caused the breach, that the attack is resolved, or that another severe incident is imminent. The commentator's Hugging Face comparison and prediction are not included.
items.dedup: Material follow-up to the already delivered October18 OpenCode breach: the new fact is the developer's account of investigation refusals and subsequent Daybreak Blue access, not the existence of the breach.
